es.summary: La nitroglicerina es un nitrato vasodilatador usado sublingualmente para el alivio agudo y la profilaxis de la angina de pecho. Actúa liberando óxido nítrico que relaja el músculo liso vascular y disminuye la demanda de oxígeno del miocardio.
key_points: Alivio rápido de la angina por dilatación venosa que reduce la precarga
Puede causar hipotensión y cefalea por vasodilatación sistémica
No usar con inhibidores de PDE‑5 ni con otros nitratos por riesgo de hipotensión grave
Tolerancia se desarrolla con uso continuo; se recomienda intervalo libre de 8‑12 h

mechanism: Se metaboliza a óxido nítrico (NO) en el torrente sanguíneo
El NO activa la guanilato ciclasa → ↑cGMP → relajación del músculo liso
Provoca dilatación venosa predominante (↓precarga) y, a dosis mayores, arterial (↓pos afterload)
Reduce la demanda de oxígeno miocárdico y mejora el flujo coronario
indications: Alivio agudo de dolor torácico por angina inestable o estable
Profilaxis de angina antes de esfuerzo físico o estrés emocional
Uso en infarto agudo de miocardio como coadyuvante al oxígeno y aspirina
contraindications: Uso concomitante de inhibidores de PDE‑5 (sildenafil, tadalafil, etc.)
Anemia severa o presión intracraneal aumentada
Hipersensibilidad a nitratos o a excipientes
interactions: Otros nitratos o nitritos → riesgo de hipotensión profunda
Antihipertensivos (beta‑bloqueadores, bloqueadores de Ca) → potenciación del efecto hipotensor
Alcohol y diuréticos → aumento de la hipotensión
nursing_care: Evaluar dolor torácico, presión arterial sistólica y frecuencia cardíaca antes de administrar
Asegurar que el paciente esté sentado o recostado; no administrar si PAS < 90 mmHg
Colocar tabletas bajo la lengua, no tragar; esperar 1‑3 min antes de repetir dosis
Monitorizar PAS, FC y aparición de cefalea cada 5 min tras la dosis
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si PAS < 90 mmHg o síncope
Documentar alivio del dolor y cualquier efecto adverso
patient_teaching: Mantener tabletas en envase original, evitar humedad
Colocar la tableta bajo la lengua y no tragar; esperar 1‑3 min antes de otra dosis
No usar más de 3 tabletas en 15 min sin indicación médica
Evitar relaciones sexuales o actividad física intensa si tomó nitrato y está usando inhibidor de PDE‑5
Reportar cefalea intensa, visión borrosa o hipotensión súbita al profesional

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de disminución de la perfusión tisular cardíaca
outcomes: Presión arterial sistólica ≥ 90 mmHg sin síntomas de hipotensión
Dolor torácico ausente o ≤ 2 en escala de 0‑10 durante 30 min después de la dosis

interventions.action: Evaluar PAS y FC antes y después de cada dosis de nitroglicerina
interventions.rationale: Detectar hipotensión o taquicardia temprana y prevenir perfusión insuficiente

interventions.action: Colocar al paciente en posición semisentada o supina antes de administrar
interventions.rationale: Reducir riesgo de síncope por hipotensión súbita

interventions.action: Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si PAS < 90 mmHg o síntomas de hipoperfusión
interventions.rationale: Evitar deterioro de la perfusión coronaria

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre evitar inhibidores de PDE‑5 y reportar cefalea intensa
interventions.rationale: Prevenir interacciones que provoquen hipotensión grave

interventions.action: Monitorear respuesta al alivio del dolor torácico y registrar escala de dolor
interventions.rationale: Asegurar eficacia del tratamiento y ajustar terapia si es necesario

en.summary: Nitroglycerin is a vasodilator nitrate used sublingually for acute relief and prophylaxis of angina pectoris. It works by releasing nitric oxide, which relaxes vascular smooth muscle and reduces myocardial oxygen demand.
key_points: Rapid relief of angina by venous dilation that reduces preload
Can cause hypotension and headache due to systemic vasodilation
Do not use with PDE‑5 inhibitors or other nitrates because of risk of severe hypotension
Tolerance develops with continuous use; an 8‑12 h drug-free interval is recommended

mechanism: Metabolized to nitric oxide (NO) in the bloodstream
NO activates guanylate cyclase → ↑cGMP → smooth muscle relaxation
Causes predominant venous dilation (↓preload) and, at higher doses, arterial dilation (↓afterload)
Reduces myocardial oxygen demand and improves coronary flow
indications: Acute relief of chest pain from unstable or stable angina
Prophylaxis of angina before physical exertion or emotional stress
Use in acute myocardial infarction as an adjunct to oxygen and aspirin
contraindications: Concurrent use of PDE‑5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, etc.)
Severe anemia or increased intracranial pressure
interactions: Other nitrates or nitrites → risk of profound hypotension
Antihypertensives (beta‑blockers, calcium channel blockers) → potentiation of hypotensive effect
nursing_care: Assess chest pain, systolic blood pressure, and heart rate before administration
Ensure patient is seated or lying down; do not administer if SBP < 90 mmHg
Place tablets under the tongue, do not swallow; wait 1‑3 min before repeating dose
Monitor SBP, HR, and onset of headache every 5 min after dose
Withhold dose and notify provider if SBP < 90 mmHg or syncope occurs
Document pain relief and any adverse effects
patient_teaching: Keep tablets in original container, avoid moisture
Place tablet under tongue and do not swallow; wait 1‑3 min before another dose
Do not use more than 3 tablets in 15 min without medical indication
Avoid sexual activity or intense physical activity if taking a nitrate and a PDE‑5 inhibitor
Report severe headache, blurred vision, or sudden hypotension to a healthcare professional

care_plans.diagnosis: Risk for decreased cardiac tissue perfusion
outcomes: Systolic blood pressure ≥ 90 mmHg without symptoms of hypotension
Chest pain absent or ≤ 2 on a 0‑10 scale within 30 min after dose

interventions.action: Assess SBP and HR before and after each nitroglycerin dose
interventions.rationale: Detect early hypotension or tachycardia and prevent inadequate perfusion

interventions.action: Place patient in semi‑recumbent or supine position before administration
interventions.rationale: Reduce risk of syncope from sudden hypotension

interventions.action: Withhold dose and notify provider if SBP < 90 mmHg or signs of hypoperfusion
Educate patient about avoiding PDE‑5 inhibitors and reporting severe headache
interventions.rationale: Prevent interactions that cause severe hypotension

interventions.action: Monitor response to chest pain relief and record pain scale
interventions.rationale: Ensure efficacy of treatment and adjust therapy if necessary

summary.0.quote: Nitroglycerin sublingual tablets are a nitrate vasodilator indicated for relief of an attack or prophylaxis of angina pectoris due to coronary artery disease.

summary.1.quote: Myocardial oxygen consumption or demand (as measured by the pressure-rate product, tension-time index, and stroke-work index) is decreased and a more favorable supply-demand ratio can be achieved.

key_points.0.quote: Dilation of postcapillary vessels, including large veins, promotes peripheral pooling of blood, decreases venous return to the heart, and reduces left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (preload).

key_points.1.quote: Nitrate overdosage may result in: severe hypotension, persistent throbbing headache, vertigo, palpitation, visual disturbance, flushing and perspiring skin (later becoming cold and cyanotic), nausea and vomiting (possibly with colic and even bloody diarrhea), syncope (especially in the upright posture), methemoglobinemia with cyanosis and anorexia, initial hyperpnea, dyspnea and slow breath

key_points.2.quote: Do not use nitroglycerin sublingual tablets in patients who are taking PDE-5 Inhibitors, such as avanafil, sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil hydrochloride.

sections.mechanism.0.quote: Nitroglycerin forms free radical nitric oxide (NO) which activates guanylate cyclase, resulting in an increase of guanosine 3'5' monophosphate (cyclic GMP) in smooth muscle and other tissues.

sections.mechanism.1.quote: Nitroglycerin forms free radical nitric oxide (NO) which activates guanylate cyclase, resulting in an increase of guanosine 3'5' monophosphate (cyclic GMP) in smooth muscle and other tissues.

sections.mechanism.2.quote: Although venous effects predominate, nitroglycerin produces, in a dose-related manner, dilation of both arterial and venous beds.

sections.mechanism.3.quote: Myocardial oxygen consumption or demand (as measured by the pressure-rate product, tension-time index, and stroke-work index) is decreased and a more favorable supply-demand ratio can be achieved.

sections.indications.0.quote: Indications For acute relief of pain in suspected acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina

sections.indications.1.quote: Nitroglycerin sublingual tablets are a nitrate vasodilator indicated for relief of an attack or prophylaxis of angina pectoris due to coronary artery disease.

sections.contraindications.0.quote: Do not use nitroglycerin sublingual tablets in patients who are taking PDE-5 Inhibitors, such as avanafil, sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil hydrochloride.

sections.contraindications.1.quote: Do not use nitroglycerin sublingual tablets in patients who are taking the soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators, such as riociguat.

sections.contraindications.2.quote: Nitroglycerin sublingual tablets are contraindicated in patients with severe anemia (large doses of nitroglycerin may cause oxidation of hemoglobin to methemoglobin and could exacerbate anemia).

sections.contraindications.3.quote: Nitroglycerin sublingual tablets are contraindicated in patients who are allergic to nitroglycerin, other nitrates or nitrites or any excipient.

sections.contraindications.4.quote: Nitroglycerin sublingual tablets are contraindicated in patients with acute circulatory failure or shock.

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: Most common adverse reactions occurring at a frequency greater than 2% are headache, dizziness and paresthesia.

sections.adverse_effects.1.quote: Flushing, drug rash, and exfoliative dermatitis have been reported in patients receiving nitrate therapy.

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: Adverse effects include orthostatic hypotension, tachycardia, paradoxical bradycardia, flushing, peripheral edema, nausea and vomiting, headache, and blurred vision.

sections.adverse_effects.3.quote: Heart rate is usually slightly increased, presumably due to a compensatory response to the fall in blood pressure.

sections.adverse_effects.5.quote: Case reports of clinically significant methemoglobinemia are rare at conventional doses of organic nitrates.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: The dose may be repeated approximately every 5 minutes, until the chest pain is relieved.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Nitroglycerin should be kept in the original glass container and must be tightly capped after each use to prevent loss of tablet potency.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: The dose may be repeated approximately every 5 minutes, until the chest pain is relieved.
